chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Ajlan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A woman performing Tamattu' Hajj arrived in Mecca and saw blood (menses), what should she do? He said: She should perform Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah and sit in her house. When she becomes pure, she performs Tawaf with the House. If she does not become pure, then when it is the Day of Tawriyah, water is poured over her, she pronounces the Talbiyah for Hajj, and goes out to Mina. She completes all the rituals. When she does that, everything becomes permissible for her except the marital bed of her husband.

And I said: Abdallah ibn Salih and I heard this Hadith in the Mosque. Abdallah went to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and came out to me, saying: I asked Abu al-Hasan about the narration of Ajlan, and he narrated to me something similar to what we heard from Ajlan.

The explanation for these two narrations is one of two things: One is that they do not indicate that her Tamattu' has been completed, and it is permissible that one in her state should act according to what both narrations contain, and her Hajj becomes Qada' (individual/single) rather than being Tamattu'. Do you not see the first narration from his saying 'When she arrives in Mecca she performs two Tawafs'? If the meaning was the completion of Tamattu', there would be three Tawafs upon her. But she is only required two Tawafs and one Sa'i because her Hajj has become individual (Qada').

His saying in the two narrations 'She performs Sa'i between Safa and Marwah' is either to be understood as recommended (Istihbab) or applied to one who wishes to return to the status of those who are Muhrim (in Ihram). For we have explained in our Great Book that whoever performs Sa'i between Safa and Marwah has become Muhrim, unless he is driving a Hady (sacrificial animal), or his command to enter Ihram for Hajj afterwards is valid, because by Sa'i she has entered the state of being Muhrim, so she needs to restart Ihram for Hajj.

The other explanation is to apply them to one who had performed more than half of the Tawaf, then saw blood. For if that is the case, she is in the position of one who has completed her Tamattu' and that is complete for her.

key_terms.أَهَلَّتْ بِالْحَج: Pronounced the Talbiyah for Hajj / Entered Ihram for Hajj
key_terms.السَّعْي: Sa'i (ritual walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَة: As-Safa and Al-Marwah (the hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.حَجَّتُهَا مُفْرَدَة: Her Hajj is individual/single (Qada' rather than Tamattu')
key_terms.حَلَّ لَهَا كُلُّ شَيْء: Everything became permissible for her (exit from Ihram restrictions)
key_terms.مُتَمِّعَةٌ: A woman performing Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّوْرِيَة: The Day of Tawriyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if she gets her period during Umrah while performing Tamattu' Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* details the specific juristic procedure for a woman in the state of Umrah Ihram who encounters menstruation, clarifying whether her Hajj remains a *Tamattu'* or transitions to a *Qada'* (compensatory) Hajj. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes that if she remains impure until the Day of Tawriyah, she performs a ritual washing, re-enters Ihram for Hajj, and completes the rites, thereby resolving the ambiguity of her ritual status. The accompanying analysis by the compiler highlights the scholarly debate on whether the initial Sa'i was obligatory or recommended, ultimately concluding that the rituals are valid either as a completed Umrah or as part of a single Hajj structure.
